seoTitle: Profit Margin Calculator - Calculate Gross Profit & Markup
metaDescription: Free profit margin calculator. Instantly calculate your gross profit, profit margin, and markup percentages based on cost and revenue.
intro: Running a business requires a clear understanding of your numbers. Our Profit Margin Calculator helps you instantly determine how much profit you're making on your products or services. Accurately calculating your profit margins enables you to make informed decisions about product lines, expansion plans, and operational changes. By removing the guesswork from your financial reporting, you can focus on building a more resilient and scalable company. Take control of your pricing strategy and maximize your bottom line with accurate data you can trust. Profitability is the lifeblood of any commercial endeavor, providing the necessary capital for reinvestment, paying off debts, and rewarding shareholders. Without a clear understanding of your profit margins, you might be unintentionally losing money on every sale, despite generating significant top-line revenue.
whatIs: This tool is a financial calculator designed to find the gross profit, profit margin, and markup percentage based on the cost of goods sold (COGS) and the final selling price (revenue).
howToUse: Enter your Cost of Goods Sold (the total cost to produce or buy the item).
Enter your Revenue (the price at which you are selling the item).
The calculator will instantly display your Gross Profit in currency.
It will also show your Profit Margin and Markup as percentages.
howItWorks: Gross profit is Revenue minus Cost. Profit Margin is Gross Profit divided by Revenue. Markup is Gross Profit divided by Cost. The tool applies these standard accounting formulas automatically.
workedExample: If you buy a product for $50 (Cost) and sell it for $100 (Revenue), your Gross Profit is $50. Your Profit Margin is 50% ($50 / $100), and your Markup is 100% ($50 / $50).
resultInterpretation: Gross Profit is your raw earnings. Profit Margin tells you how much out of every dollar of sales you keep as gross profit. Markup tells you how much you increased the cost price to arrive at the selling price.
useCases: Retail: Pricing new inventory to ensure a healthy bottom line.
E-commerce: Determining if a product is viable after wholesale and shipping costs.
Freelancing: Calculating the profit margin on project-based services.
tipsAndLimitations: This calculator determines 'Gross' profit margin, not 'Net' margin (which would include overhead, taxes, and operating expenses).
Don't confuse Margin and Markup; a 100% markup only equals a 50% margin.

faq.question: What is the difference between profit margin and markup?
faq.answer: Profit margin is based on the selling price (revenue), showing the percentage of sales that is profit. Markup is based on the cost, showing how much the cost was increased to reach the selling price.

faq.question: What is a good profit margin?
faq.answer: A 'good' margin varies wildly by industry. Grocery stores might operate on 2% net margins, while software companies might have 80% gross margins. 10% net margin is generally considered average across many industries.

disclaimer: This tool provides calculations for informational purposes. Always consult with a financial professional for business accounting.
